provenance: model_supplied; no operator witness is asserted
authority: Interpretation and acceptance design only. T-442 and the existing T-443 through T-451 authorization remain controlling.

clauses.text: Provide one command or UI action that starts the authorized parallel worker pool for SAIPEN engineering. Source asks for one click or command. T-442 and T-443/T-444 admission remain required.
SAIPEN assigns distinct eligible task or audit generations autonomously. Bind each assignment to exact Source bytes and one current owner; duplicate delivery cannot assign the same generation twice.
Use separate Git worktrees for engineering workers, with separate indexes and bounded writable scope. Prove source isolation before concurrent edits. Source explicitly requests worktrees.

Parallel workers perform actual engineering improvements to admitted SAIPEN tasks or audits and produce source patches. Read-only research or a toy arithmetic demonstration cannot satisfy this request.

clauses.origin: proposed durability elaboration; existing T-448 design
clauses.text: Proposed acceptance R5: each worker durably checkpoints identity, assignment generation, owned changes, verification status and remaining work independently of chat. Original source does not explicitly specify this recovery format.

clauses.origin: proposed durability elaboration; existing T-448 design
clauses.text: Proposed acceptance R6: worker loss, provider limit or restart preserves accepted work. This is a proposed operational completion criterion, not evidence that failover exists or authority to implement before admission.

clauses.origin: proposed recovery elaboration; existing T-448 design
clauses.text: Proposed acceptance R7: a fresh replacement resumes the same assignment from durable verified progress without repeating unchanged completed checks. Prove an actual model-session restart after lawful admission.

Engineering handbacks are immutable patch-and-evidence proposals bound to base source identity, worker, Work, declared resources and verification. Reuse ProducerPackage and the existing Core integration owners rather than creating an incompatible format.

Refuse stale proposals and conflicting read/write or logical-resource claims before canonical mutation. Preserve refused proposals and their evidence; never silently rebase or merge changed dependencies.

clauses.origin: existing T-444 and canonical single writer
clauses.text: One canonical Core integrator accepts eligible proposals sequentially through the existing writer lock and journal. Workers do not become concurrent authors of canonical STATE, BOARD or LOG.

Each accepted engineering proposal requires independent verification on the relevant source generation and the mandatory integration gates. A worker cannot approve its own handback or replace complete required regression coverage with focused tests.

clauses.origin: existing Source and audit generation closure
clauses.text: Consume an audit only through exact-generation Source closure and the canonical audit delete gate after linked Work is terminal. Patch acceptance alone never authorizes Source deletion.
Proposed acceptance R13: worker count is configurable with an initial two-worker milestone; twelve is not a source requirement. The original Source gives no fixed pool size.

Proposed acceptance R14: resource pressure bounds simultaneous tests and builds independently of worker count. Benchmark 1, 2 and 4 only after capabilities exist; no worker-per-family multiplication without evidence.

clauses.origin: proposed operability elaboration; existing T-448 monitor
clauses.text: Proposed acceptance R15: inspect assignments, generation, progress, blockers and accepted results through local files or a command. No GUI, database or proprietary runtime is required for authority or recovery.

Keep ordinary sequential SAIPEN operation available and authoritative while the admitted pool operates. Concurrent Mode is the existing future saipen concurrent concept; saipen crew remains the serial circuit.

clauses.origin: existing Core and producer authority boundary
clauses.text: An engineering worker cannot independently modify canonical authority, collect its own output, grant a lease, integrate, ship or consume an audit. Worktree isolation does not itself prove a protected mutation boundary.

Proposed acceptance R18: a finished worker receives another eligible audit through a fresh durable assignment generation without retaining old write authority. The original request implies autonomous distribution but does not specify the reuse protocol.

clauses.origin: direct source outcome omitted from proposed R1-R18
clauses.text: Use the operator-configured available models, subscriptions and agents through evidence-backed host capabilities and eligibility policy. Do not invent a supported model, effort, account credential, subscription or unapproved external action.
